Silhouette: Very large cat frame, longer and heavier than either parent, long body, heavy forequarters, small or no mane. Host frame: the lion sets the outline, body size and overall frame. A single creature combining a lion and a tiger. Head of the lion, fully visible and uncluttered, with clear, discernible eyes. Details: behavior: social lion-like behavior may follow one parent without full performance behind it; body: long, heavy intermediate cat body with heavy forequarters; coat color: tawny lion-like base, incomplete-dominance blend leaning to sire; faint tiger pattern at about 20 percent strength on the flanks and legs; coat pattern: faint tiger stripes diluted because body is not tiger-owned, overlay on tawny base; coat texture: short, dense coat from tiger; ears: rounded intermediate ears leaning to lion, shifted with face; face: lion-like muzzle and face, same neural-crest group as ears; feet: lion-like feet consistent with head and forequarter group; head: lion-like head shape; limbs: intermediate limb proportions near midpoint; mane: reduced mane or none in males, never full mane with full-strength stripes; skull: skull proportions intermediate leaning to lion with face and ears; tail: intermediate tail length near midpoint. Pattern lines and texture flow follow the body outline. Bilaterally symmetrical, recognizable limbs, visible sense organs. Habitat cue (grassland): plainer coat with fewer markings for an open habitat. One creature, full body, side three-quarter view, plain light background, natural history illustration.
Aspect ratio: 1:1.
